summary:
Bermuda is a British Overseas Territory whose local legislation governs; the United Kingdom's Equality Act 2010 and its 2025 single-sex services code do not automatically extend here and could be applied only by Order in Council.

There is no legal recognition of transgender people in Bermuda, and the sources identify no transgender-specific provisions on documents, screening, facilities, custody, healthcare, penalties or protection machinery. The Human Rights Act's discrimination protection, in force for sexual orientation since 2013, does not extend to gender identity, leaving trans people without statutory protection against discrimination.

Expression of gender identity is described as often difficult. In 2006 the Government attempted to bar Mark Anderson, the drag performer known as "Queen of Bermuda" Sybil, from a parade, stating that he contradicted local mores and sensitivities.

Consensual sex between adult men was decriminalised by the House of Assembly on 14 May 1994, by a vote of 22–16, striking two sections of the Criminal Code; the debate divided the island, with religious leaders split and the Christian Coalition staging marches against the change. Prior liability had carried up to ten years' imprisonment for anal and oral sex. The gross indecency provision between men was repealed in 2019. As of 2022 the age of consent stands at 18 for consensual anal intercourse under the law effective 1 November 2019, against 16 for other sexual activity.

Same-sex marriage is not legally available as of 2022. The Supreme Court legalised it in May 2017 in the Godwin and DeRoche case; the Governor gave assent to the Domestic Partnership Act on 7 February 2018, effective 1 June 2018, replacing marriage with domestic partnerships open to same-sex and opposite-sex couples and making Bermuda the first jurisdiction to revoke marriage equality. The Supreme Court restored marriage on 6 June 2018 and the Court of Appeal on 23 November 2018, but the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council banned it again on 14 March 2022, with July 2022 laws retrospectively backdating prior legality. Recognition of a partner therefore rests on the partnership register.

Organised religious hostility toward visible same-sex couples is documented: in July the AME church and other Bermuda churches protested a gay cruise as "incompatible with the word of God and the Christian moral fibre".

Same-sex couples may adopt on equal terms under the Adoption of Children Act following the February 2015 Supreme Court ruling on marital-status and sexual-orientation discrimination, and binational same-sex partners were granted equal employment and benefits by the Supreme Court in November 2015.

The Bermuda Regiment, raised by random lottery conscription, officially prohibits discrimination or harassment of LGBT soldiers, though such conduct has been reported as tolerated by officers to the extent that one conscript described the Regiment as "the most homophobic environment that exists".

Gay and bisexual men may donate blood through the Bermuda Hospitals Board if they have not had sex with another man in the past 12 months; a 12-month deferral likewise applies to women who have sex with men who have sex with men.

In November 2020 reporting, the government spent approximately £150,000 to appeal the case of a man charged and threatened with jail under the "obscene behaviour law" for importing gay porn DVDs, a case held unconstitutional.
tangentialFactors:
The 1994 decriminalisation vote and the 2018 marriage reversal both followed sustained campaigning by the Christian Coalition and affiliated churches, indicating that religious lobbying remains a live force in legislative outcomes affecting sexual minorities.

The 2006 attempt to bar a drag performer from a parade, and the reported tolerance of homophobic conduct inside the Bermuda Regiment, sit alongside formal non-discrimination rules, showing a gap between written policy and practice.

Bermuda's trajectory on relationship recognition has reversed three times at the highest appellate level, from Supreme Court to Court of Appeal to the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council, so the current position rests on a final judgment rather than settled statute alone.

The age of consent is 18 for consensual anal intercourse and 16 for other sexual activity. Blood donation through the Bermuda Hospitals Board carries a 12-month deferral for gay and bisexual men and an equivalent deferral for women who have sex with men who have sex with men.
